The core at mihomo v1.19.33, with 18 TCP fixes in the stack both tunnels run on; a settings page that answers at once; the detector files each site the moment its own checks end and tries the ClientHello cut on more blocks.

To update, run the new `dpiswitch.exe` from anywhere and accept the offer to install over the installed version (one administrator prompt). Settings, lists, configs and verdicts are kept.

## Core

- **mihomo v1.19.33.** The stack every tunnelled TCP connection runs on (mipstack) comes with 18 fixes since the last core: stalls with high-frequency TCP timestamps, a keepalive timeout firing early, a connection's close waiting on a blocked write, zero-window and loss-recovery accounting. The TUN adapter's library goes to sing-tun 0.4.28.
- **A DoH request the core gave up on ends on its own**, instead of piling up connections to a server that does not answer.

## Interface

- **Settings answer at once.** What the pages are drawn from — the settings, both tunnels' configs, the lists — is kept in memory and read again only when its file changes; the service's state is gathered in the background. A setting saved shows in 10–15 ms, the header's mode with it (it followed 150–650 ms late), and the first change after the tray starts is as quick as the rest (it took over half a second).
- **The settings are six groups that open and close on their titles** — Detector, Terms, DPI bypass, Network, Program and DNS — all closed as the window opens; the groups open stay open as the form is redrawn, and a link to a setting opens its group.
- **Every hint in the settings starts at the left**, at one size: a short one stood in the middle of its column.
- **The header names the build** — "v1.12.1" and the commit it was built from, a "+" for a build with changes not committed. The service's and the tray's logs and the tray's title carry it too.
- **The header's awg2 shows a slow tunnel in yellow**, as awg1's does.

## Detector

- **A site's verdict lands the moment its own checks end**, not when the slowest site checked beside it is done: habr.com, ria.ru and stackoverflow.com waited 70 s behind another site whose tunnel did not answer.
- **Every new site gets a place in the fast lane** (twelve, sixteen for QUIC checked ahead), and is picked up the moment it is seen. **Connections too short for the table to show** — meduza.io, www.linkedin.com — are seen through the core's log and checked too.
- **A site's ports, and its IPv6 node beside its IPv4 one, are checked at once**: one after another a blocked host took about a minute.
- **The ClientHello cut is tried on more blocks**: a node that drops every hello (rutracker.org's), a handshake failing both direct and through the tunnel (www.newtimes.ru), any inconclusive site whose direct hello failed (www.sibreal.org). Each goes direct with the cut only on its own verified answer.
- **The cut prefers IPv4**: it got through on a site's IPv4 node and was dropped on its IPv6 one — www.youtube.com, play.google.com, signal.org among 24 sites — and the worse node sent the site through the tunnel.
- **A session cut after the cut's handshake** (zona.media) is the cut not getting through, and is judged so.
- **A site that answers us differently from the tunnel over a verified TLS chain is the server's own difference** — a redirect, a bot check for a data centre — not a block: hh.ru, www.cian.ru and tass.ru went through the tunnel.
- **A site whose TCP is refused while its QUIC gets through the decoy goes direct over QUIC**, and is checked again on a block's schedule.
- **CDN families are read from five hosts each, not one**, and are kept over rounds: googlevideo.com's ISP-cache nodes had cost YouTube its family. A round waits for the tunnel to answer first, and a CDN that cannot be read backs off instead of being asked every ten minutes.
- **A check made under settings changed meanwhile is made again**, not filed.
- **A dead direct connection makes its site a suspect once**, not every cycle it stays open.

## Service

- **A refused "forget" request is removed at once**, not a second later.
- **Network adapters are read in one call**, and the inherited ranges are joined once per change, not on every sync.

Core: the fork's 6027ebb8 (mihomo v1.19.33, Alpha 3f27ef39).
